keyword: how to become a data analyst after 10th
title: How to Become a Data Analyst After 10th (2026)
desc: How to become a data analyst after Class 10: SQL, statistics, dashboards and data storytelling, with a yearly plan, projects, certificates and salary.
h1: How to become a data analyst after 10th
SQL, dashboards and a clear plan
lead: A plan for a Class 10 student and their parent to read together. Most analyst skills sit in year 1 of a real 624-hour data curriculum. This page shows what that year teaches and what comes after.
role_intro: A data analyst turns a company's records into answers people can act on. They write SQL to pull data, check it with statistics, build dashboards and charts, and explain in plain words what changed and why. It is often the first job in the data field.
in_short: A data analyst answers "what happened, and why?" The daily work is SQL queries, checking numbers and explaining them in charts and short notes.
The analyst toolkit sits almost entirely in year 1: SQL, two statistics modules, Pandas, visualisation, business analytics and dashboards.
Accuracy and clear writing count as much as coding. One wrong join can mislead a team, and a plain summary is what managers act on.
start_answer: Yes. You can start after Class 10, because analyst work rests on SQL and school-level statistics, both taught from zero in year 1, and these are enough to answer real questions about real tables.

day_to_day.answer: A data analyst spends most days pulling data with SQL, checking it for errors, working out what changed and why, and explaining the answer through charts, dashboards and short written summaries.
day_to_day.html:
Work usually starts with a question from sales, marketing, finance or operations, such as "why did orders drop last week?" The analyst writes SQL to pull the right rows, cleans gaps and duplicates, and compares periods and groups. Then they check whether a change is real or just noise. The answer goes out as a chart, a dashboard update or a short note that also states its limits.

The main tools in this roadmap are SQL, Python with Pandas and NumPy, and Jupyter notebooks, with Git and GitHub to keep work saved and shareable. Many offices also use spreadsheets and business intelligence tools. The program does not list Excel, Power BI or Tableau, so practise a spreadsheet on your own.

How it differs from a data scientist. An analyst explains the past and present: what happened, where and why. A data scientist also builds machine learning models that predict what comes next, which needs more maths and coding. In this program, the analyst toolkit is year 1, and machine learning starts in year 2. The data scientist page covers that longer path.

first_project.answer: A realistic first project is a two-to-three-week study of data you collect yourself, such as your daily screen time or sleep, ending in two clear charts and a one-page summary that answers one question.
first_project.html:
Pick one question you care about, such as "on which days do I use my phone most?" Then:

  • Week 1 and 2: record the data every day in one simple table, or use a small public dataset instead.
  • Week 2: clean it. Fix missing days, wrong entries and mixed units, and write down every fix.
  • Week 3: work out averages and totals by day of the week, and find the highest and lowest days.
  • Week 3: make two charts, one showing change over time and one comparing groups.
  • Finish with a one-page summary: the answer, the evidence, and what the data cannot tell you.

A spreadsheet is enough to start. If you have begun learning SQL or Python, redo the totals in code. This is a small version of the program's Exploratory Statistics Report and Data Storytelling Report, both in year 1.

B.Tech through JEE Main needs Physics and Mathematics, so that route closes.
B.Tech, BCA and B.Sc in statistics or computer science. Opens analyst and later data science roles.
A heavier study load. Analysis practice has to fit around entrance preparation.
Economics, psychology and social science degrees, which feed policy and research analysis.
Without any maths in Class 11 and 12, statistics feels harder. Keep Mathematics or Economics if you can.
start_extra: The stream matters less for analysts than for engineers. Employers mostly want proof that you can query data, check it and explain it. A small set of finished analysis projects shows that better than marks alone.
roadmap_answer: For a data analyst, year 1 does most of the work: Python, SQL, two statistics modules, visualisation, business analytics and dashboards, while years 2 and 3 add forecasting, data pipelines and experimentation for stronger analyst roles.
year_focus: Year 1: the core analyst toolkit, from SQL and statistics to dashboards
Year 2: forecasting, segmentation and the data pipelines analysts depend on
Year 3: experimentation, advanced analytics and a portfolio that tells stories
fit_note: This program serves both analysts and data scientists. Years 2 and 3 cover machine learning and AI that a pure analyst may not use daily. Its listed tools are Python, SQL, Git, GitHub, Linux, NumPy, Pandas, Jupyter and Azure. It does not list Excel, Power BI or Tableau, so practise a spreadsheet tool on your own as well.
skills_answer: A data analyst needs SQL, statistics, data cleaning, Python with Pandas, charts and dashboards, business sense, simple forecasting and, above all, the ability to tell a clear story from the numbers.
skills: The daily tool for pulling and joining company data.
Averages, spread, sampling and tests: how you know a change is real.
Real data has gaps and errors. Cleaning comes before any answer.
Picking the chart that makes the point obvious.

build_answer: You build one project every month, and the first twelve already form an analyst portfolio: SQL work, statistics reports, cleaned datasets, a business case, a dashboard and a capstone.
projects: A public set of queries that proves you can work with real tables.
Your first written report that explains data with numbers.
Shows the unglamorous skill every analyst job needs.
Practice turning a chart into a decision someone can make.
A business question answered from start to finish.
A dashboard a manager could open each morning.
A complete case in the style of the Google Data Analytics certificate.
A test of whether a product change worked, a common analyst task.
certs_answer: For analysts, the Google Data Analytics certificate and Microsoft DP-900 are the most relevant in this roadmap, but each is awarded by its own body, and employers will still ask to see your analysis work.

cert_notes.Google Data Analytics Professional Certi: A 9-course series on Coursera covering data cleaning, analysis and visualisation with spreadsheets, SQL and other tools. Google says no degree or prior experience is needed.
cert_notes.Microsoft Certified: Azure Data Fundamen: A beginner exam on core data concepts, relational and non-relational data, and analytics workloads on Azure. Microsoft aims it at people starting with data in the cloud.

cert_extra: Both the Google certificate and DP-900 are prepared for in year 1, which is why an analyst can build a credible profile early.
notfor_answer: This path is not for you if you dislike checking details, want to avoid writing and presenting, or expect analysis to be all coding, because much of the job is careful checking and clear explaining.
notfor: Small mistakes in numbers do not bother you.
Analysts are trusted for accuracy. One wrong join can mislead a whole team.
Reports, charts and short talks are a big part of the role.
You want to build apps, not study data.
The Software Development program fits that better.
No honest course can promise a job, salary or exam pass, and this one does not.
You can only study now and then.
Plan for 4 hours of classes a week for three years, plus practice.
salary_answer: Indicative ranges for data roles in India, including analysts, are about ₹4 to 8 lakh a year for freshers, ₹10 to 22 lakh at 3 to 5 years, and ₹25 to 50 lakh or more at senior level.
faqs: How many years does it take to become a data analyst after 10th?

The core analyst skills come in year 1 of the 3-year, 624-hour Data Science & AI program, and the next two years build depth. Many employers also expect a degree, so most people reach an analyst job after Class 12 and a degree, with skills built alongside.
Can I become a data analyst without maths?

Yes, more easily than in most data roles, because analysts mainly use school-level statistics, which the program teaches in two modules. Keeping Mathematics or Economics in Class 11 and 12 still makes statistics much easier and keeps more degrees open.
Is a data analyst the same as a data scientist?

No. A data analyst explains what happened and why, using SQL, statistics and dashboards. A data scientist also builds machine learning models to predict what comes next. Many people start as analysts and move into data science later.
Do I need coding to become a data analyst?
Some, yes. SQL is essential, and Python with Pandas helps with larger or messier data. Both are taught from the beginning in year 1, so no prior coding is expected.
Can a commerce student become a data analyst?
Yes. Commerce with Mathematics is a strong base for business and finance analysis. What matters most is proof that you can query, clean and explain data.
context_fact: Nasscom's Strategic Review 2026 puts employment in India's tech industry near 6 million. Analysts who can explain data clearly are useful across that whole industry, not only in tech teams.
